platform: physical Apple M4, macOS 27.0.1, native ARM64 release, eight-worker shared CPU pool, unbound scheduling
retained_change: Automatic NEON recognition uses eight stable line owners for at least eight independent units and context capacity >= 8; sparse, explicit and non-NEON policies retain base budgets. No kernel edits retained.

timing_budget.expansion_reason: Separate the retained scheduling policy from the kernel candidate, validate all three models on dense input plus concurrent requests and the sparse Tiny case. Fixed seven cells, no retries or sampling growth.

rejected_variants.cache_groups: 48/96/192 rows had overlapping kernel timing ranges on representative shapes; keep 48.
rejected_variants.four_row_tiles: No consistent full-tile benefit; not retained.
rejected_variants.exact_row_tails: Four-row kernel improved from 0.054833 to 0.035833 ms in the rebuilt diagnostic, but twelve OCR comparisons all overlapped. Scheduling-only retained for smaller change; no short_tile symbol in final benchmark.

validation.clippy: Passed with existing architecture-specific unused/dead-code and harness-style warnings.

run.build: standard release; default features; automatic SIMD/layout; fusion enabled

limits: Three fixed samples and one warmup do not establish statistical significance or steady state.
Tiny sparse median was 4.84% slower with disjoint sampled ranges despite unchanged worker selection; cause is not established.
Concurrent throughput ranges overlap in all three retained cases; no established throughput gain.
Additional recognition arenas increase peak resident memory, by up to 19.03% in the selected cases.
Only dense inputs for all three models plus sparse Tiny are measured on final source; earlier mixed-input results include a rejected kernel and are not final-source evidence.
No fresh C# performance-parity claim; live C# qualification is correctness only.
No native x86 performance measurement; runtime policy is gated by the NEON backend.
